title: Five risks, one family
subtitle: What each would cost, as a what-if
note: The family is Antevo’s example household: CHF 35.5m in five portfolios at three made-up banks. The risks are Antevo’s list of the date shown. Every figure is the Antevo Wealth tool’s answer. A what-if is not a forecast.

tries.label: Today’s list, risk by risk
tries.source: Antevo Wealth, 25 Nov 2026. Each risk is tied to one named what-if from a fixed list that Antevo keeps. A what-if is not a forecast: the risk may play out differently, or not at all. A risk with no fitting what-if gets no figure.

items.name: Tariffs reach spring prices with no stockpile
evidence: What-if: Stagflation, prices that keep rising while growth stalls
Growth −19.8%, Funds −16.2%, Nasdaq fund −16.1%, Balanced −14.0%, Capital Preservation −9.7%

items.name: New tariffs on the largest trading partners
evidence: Growth −10.2%, Funds −9.2%, Nasdaq fund −7.8%, Balanced −3.8%, Capital Preservation +1.1%

items.name: AI suppliers lose their second bid
evidence: What-if: Sector Rotation, technology −15% and cheaper shares +10%
Nasdaq fund −10.4%, Growth −9.1%, Balanced −3.7%, Funds −2.1%, Capital Preservation −0.2%

items.name: A firm inflation figure restores hike bets
evidence: What-if: interest rates two points higher
Capital Preservation −1.2%, Balanced −0.6%, the other three portfolios unchanged

items.name: The Gulf truce frays at sea and in Riyadh
evidence: No what-if on Antevo’s list stands for this risk
That is not the same as no effect

items.do: Read the cost, not the headline
items.why: The risk in the news, the trade war, costs a third of what rising prices with no growth would.

items.do: Look at each portfolio against each risk
items.why: The cautious portfolio gains in one what-if and loses a tenth in another.

items.do: Ask the same question next week
items.why: The list changes every morning; the figures follow what you own that day.

items.do: Read the story behind each line
items.why: What the risk is, whether it is rising, and what to watch.

items.do: Know what is inside your funds first
items.why: A what-if is only as good as the picture of what you own.

sections.title: The cautious portfolio
sections.so_what: A label says what a portfolio is for, not what it is protected against.
evidence: Interest rates two points higher: −1.2%, more than any other portfolio

sections.title: Higher interest rates
sections.verdict: A small figure is a finding too
sections.so_what: This family holds few bonds, so higher rates on their own cost it little.
evidence: Three of the five portfolios do not move

sections.title: Past crashes, replayed
sections.verdict: The worst case is not on today’s list
sections.so_what: Today’s list is what is in the news now. The replays show what the holdings have been through before.
evidence: A replay of the crash of 2000 to 2002: growth portfolio −61%, Nasdaq fund −67%
A replay is not a forecast

sections.title: How a risk gets its figure
sections.verdict: A fixed list, not a guess
sections.so_what: The answer says which what-if it used, so you can disagree with the choice.
evidence: Each risk is tied to one named what-if from a fixed list that Antevo keeps. A what-if is not a forecast: the risk may play out differently, or not at all. A risk with no fitting what-if gets no figure.

links.text: Tariffs appear twice on the list. As a trade war they cost 5.3% of everything; as rising prices with no growth, 15.0%. The same news, two what-ifs.
The portfolio that falls most when technology goes out of favour is the fund at the third bank, not the single shares at the first.
